evidence_quotes.quote: The Kenyan water policy framework recognizes WRUAs as the legal, grassroots collective action
line to generate a water poverty dummy where Water poor = 1, and Water non-poor = 0.
With regards to water, members have better access to both domestic and irrigation water,
8%, income poor by about 47%, subjective poor by about 20% and water poor by about 14%.
Holding a title deed had a positive influence on WRUA membership.

headline_result_summary: Examining 652 rural smallholder farm households in Kenya's Upper Ewaso Ng'iro North Catchment Area, Mwaura et al. (2021) evaluate the impact of membership in legally institutionalized Water Resource Users Associations (WRUAs, recognized under Kenya's Water Act 2002 and Water Act 2016) on multidimensional poverty, including a polychoric PCA-based household Water Poverty Index binary outcome (1 = water poor [<40th percentile of water security], 0 = water non-poor). Across all treatment-effect specifications in Table 7, WRUA membership significantly reduces the probability of household water poverty: the Endogenous Switching Probit (ESP) average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) is -0.140 (SE = 0.071; z = -1.97, p approx. 0.049), the Propensity Score Matching (4-nearest-neighbor) ATT is -0.323 (SE = 0.044, p < 0.01) and the Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) ATT is -0.303 (SE = 0.038, p < 0.01). Because the outcome is water poverty (higher = worse water security/access), these negative estimates translate into a substantive improvement in household water access/security (favorable_to_access), corroborated by large descriptive advantages for WRUA members in compound piped water coverage (82.8% vs. 21.5%) and shorter domestic water collection time (3.30 vs. 20.44 minutes). As a secondary legal variable, holding a land title deed positively predicts joining a WRUA (probit beta = 0.405, SE = 0.139, p < 0.01) but has no statistically significant direct effect on water poverty within either membership regime (0.160 [SE = 0.188] for members; 0.100 [SE = 0.168] for non-members).
specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. Inverse outcome polarity on the primary model: The econometrically modeled water outcome is 'Water poverty' (1 = water poor, 0 = water non-poor), so negative treatment effects (ESP ATT = -0.140, PSM ATT = -0.323, IPW ATT = -0.303) represent reductions in water poverty, i.e., favorable_to_access. Confusing 'Water poverty' with the 'Water security index' from which it is cut off would invert the substantive direction. 2. Reversed subtraction order in descriptive Tables 2 and 3: In Tables 2 and 3 (PDF Pages 10-11), 'Mean difference' is calculated as (Non-members minus WRUA members), even though WRUA members are listed in the first column. Thus WRUA members having 82.8% piped water vs. 21.5% for non-members is printed as Mean difference = -0.613*** (t = -19.812), and lower water poverty among members (23.36% vs. 52.34%) is printed as +0.291*** (t = 8.021). Reading the sign of the 'Mean difference' column without checking the group means would flip the direction. 3. Over-starred significance and typographical errors in hypotheses/tables: On PDF Page 5, the authors state four hypotheses of a 'positive relationship' between poverty and WRUA membership, then on PDF Pages 16-17 write 'We therefore reject all four hypotheses that there is no relationship'. In Table 7 (PDF Page 17), ESP ATT (-0.140, SE = 0.071 -> z = -1.97, p approx. 0.049) and ATU (-0.109, SE = 0.066 -> z = -1.65, p approx. 0.099) on water poverty are both marked '***' (1%) despite having p-values near 0.05 and 0.10 respectively, and IPW ATT on subjective poverty is printed as '0.091**' missing its minus sign (contradicting p. 16 text stating a ~9% reduction). 4. Endogeneity/circularity in the WPI index and exclusion restrictions: Table A2 (PDF Page 22) includes 'Piped water', 'Sanitation facility', 'Owning land', 'Title' and 'Water Conflict' inside the components used to construct the Water Poverty Index, while 'Water conflict', 'MWS-River' and 'MWS-Borehole' are used as exclusion-restriction instruments in the first-stage WRUA selection model (and 'MWS-Piped water' was dropped after failing the falsification test in Table A1). Also, if a coder extracts 'Title' (land title deed) instead of WRUA membership, Title is positive and significant for WRUA participation (Table 5: 0.405***) but null in the second-stage Water poverty outcome equations (Table 6: 0.160 and 0.100).
study_design: Cross-sectional observational household survey (conducted September–December 2019) using multistage sampling, analyzed with a Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML) Endogenous Switching Probit (ESP) model alongside Propensity Score Matching (PSM, 4 nearest neighbors) and Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) treatment-effect estimators
unit_and_sample_size: Rural smallholder farm households across 8 sampled sub-catchments in the Upper Ewaso Ng'iro North Catchment Area; N = 652 households (331 WRUA members and 321 non-members)
